narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the recent sharp rise in global average temperatures and attribute it to human fossil fuel consumption, contrasting it with long-term historical stability.

units.meaning: Before the first positive reading, the anomaly series stays negative and only ranges from -0.4320 to -0.0160, a span of 0.4160; this is the long early stretch of no zero-crossing.

basis.note: lowest value before the first positive reading
closest-to-zero value before the first positive reading

accepted_routes: Before the first positive reading, the series stays between -0.4320 and -0.0160, a range of 0.4160 anomaly units.
The early portion never reaches zero and varies only within about 0.42 anomaly units.
All readings before the first positive value are negative, from about -0.43 up to about -0.02.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The early portion must remain below zero and not exceed the small negative value near -0.016 before the first positive point.
units.temporal_anchor: For more than 10,000 years, the average global temperature didn't change by more than one degree Celsius.
units.reviewer_question: Should the early negative/no-crossing band be a required beat for long-term stability, or is general pre-rise stability enough?

units.meaning: The first positive anomaly in the series is 0.0520, marking a zero-crossing after the previous value of -0.0160.

basis.note: immediately prior value, still below zero

accepted_routes: The first positive anomaly appears as 0.0520 after the series has stayed below zero.
The plotted series crosses the zero line just before a reading of 0.0520.
Before the first positive reading, the closest value is -0.0160; then it goes to 0.0520.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A zero crossing must be visible, with the first positive plotted value at 0.0520.
units.temporal_anchor: But then humans started burning fossil fuels around here.
units.reviewer_question: Is the first zero-crossing essential to the contrast, or just a fluctuation before the post-1950 rise?

units.meaning: At the 1950-marked reference point, the anomaly is -0.0980, still negative; this is not yet the modern high.
accepted_routes: At the 1950 marker, the anomaly value is -0.0980, still below zero.
The point labeled 1950 reads -0.098, so the rise is not yet underway in that row.
Around 1950 the series is slightly negative, at about -0.10 anomaly units.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 1950 time marker must be identifiable and show a value below zero.
units.reviewer_question: Should the 1950 marker be an explicit required anchor, or is it optional context?

units.meaning: From the 1950-marked value (-0.0980) to the final value (0.9460), the anomaly rises by 1.0440, about one unit on the table's anomaly scale.
accepted_routes: Since the 1950 marker, the value rises from -0.0980 to 0.9460, an increase of 1.0440.
The 1950-to-final change is about 1.0 anomaly unit (0.9460 minus -0.0980).
The anomaly climbs by roughly 1.04 from the 1950 point to the end.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show both the 1950 point (below zero) and the final endpoint (0.9460), or make the difference 1.0440 visually comparable.
units.temporal_anchor: Today global temperatures have risen about one degree Celsius since pre-
units.reviewer_question: Is the recent rise required to be quantified as the 1950-to-final increase of 1.0440, or can the video just show a sharp upward shape?

units.meaning: The final reading is the series maximum: value 0.9460 and relative_value 1.0000, the highest normalized value in the table.
accepted_routes: The series ends at its highest value, 0.9460, with relative_value 1.0000.
The final point is the maximum of the series; its normalized size is 1.0000.
The last reading is the largest, at 0.9460 and relative maximum 1.0000.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The final plotted value must be visibly the highest of the series.
units.reviewer_question: Is the final maximum required as its own beat, or is it sufficiently carried by the 1950-to-end rise?

optional_valid: The series has earlier positive blips, including a local maximum of 0.1440, before returning to -0.0980 at the 1950 marker.
The first positive reading 0.0520 is followed by later dips below zero before the sustained post-1950 rise.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that fossil fuel burning caused the temperature rise; the table contains no fossil fuel data.
The 10,000-year duration as a table fact.
Exact Celsius labeling or exact 1 degree Celsius as a table value when the table unit column is blank.
Any percentage share of warming attributed to fossil fuels.
Values or baselines not present in the table, such as a pre-industrial baseline beyond the rows shown.
notes: The table contains one temperature-anomaly series; absolute numbers are in value, while relative_value is only a 0-1 normalization for size/order. Fossil-fuel attribution and the 10,000-year span appear only in the narration, not in the table, so they should not be encoded as data units.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
